correctness.rationale: For a species of census size a, exact sampling yields \(a\binom{N-a}{k-1}/\binom Nk\) expected singleton indicator. The verified forward-difference and second-difference identities establish a discrete concave-to-convex kernel. Concentrating pairs above the trough and balancing pairs below it cannot decrease the sum, providing a globally maximizing canonical integer profile and the exact one-dimensional envelope. Uniform exponential tails for \((ak/N)\binom{N-k}{a-1}/\binom{N-1}{a-1}\) give uniform convergence to \(a\rho(1-\rho)^{a-1}\); the unique integer maximizer away from reciprocal rho and a positive gap prove eventual uniqueness at fixed S. Checked all small parameter boundaries and direct sample enumeration with exact arithmetic. No statement of asymptotic uniqueness at reciprocal rho or growing S.

value.rationale: Expected sampled-singleton counts are an established indicator of ecological undersampling and are ingredients of sample coverage estimators. For fixed true species richness and total individuals, the maximum of this statistic is a natural model-free baseline. The structural theorem collapses the integer-partition search to O(N) candidates and the fixed-S large-census theorem identifies a sharp staircase of optimally detectable rare abundances as sample fraction changes. These are motivated mathematical bounds, not merely tiny finite examples, and limitations on model and parameter regimes are explicit.
